facts.statement: Sanchiaosaurus is an extinct basal nothosauroid from the Middle Triassic of Guizhou Province in southwestern China.
facts.quote: Sanchiaosaurus is an extinct genus of a basal nothosauroid known from the Middle Triassic (Anisian age) of Guizhou Province, southwestern China.

facts.statement: The genus Sanchiaosaurus contains only one species, Sanchiaosaurus dengi.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Sanchiaosaurus dengi.

facts.statement: Sanchiaosaurus is known only from a single partial skeleton, the holotype IVPP V3228, kept at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: Sanchiaosaurus is known solely from the holotype IVPP V3228, a partial skeleton housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sanchiaosaurus were found near Guiyang in Guizhou Province from the Guanling Formation, dating to the Anisian stage of the early Middle Triassic, approximately 245 million years ago.
facts.quote: IVPP V.3228 was collected near the Jinzhong Bridge, in the suburbs of Guiyang City, Chinchungchiao, Sanchiao in the vicinity of Guiyang, Guizhou Province, from the first member of the Guanling Formation, dating to the Anisian stage of the early Middle Triassic, about 245 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus was first described and named by Yang Zhongjian (Chung-Chien Young) in 1965.
facts.quote: Sanchiaosaurus was first described and named by Yang Zhongjian, also known as Chung-Chien Young, in 1965

facts.statement: The name Sanchiaosaurus combines the locality name Sanchiao with the Greek word sauros meaning lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Sanchiao, in reference to the locality where the holotype was found, and from Greek sauros, meaning "lizard", a common suffix for genus names of extinct reptile.

facts.statement: Sanchiaosaurus belongs to the parent group Nothosauroidea.
Sanchiaosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: The holotype skeleton preserves the skull, lower jaw, one isolated tooth, and a partially preserved postcranial skeleton viewed from below.
rejected.quote: This skeleton is exposed in ventral view, i.e. from below, and preserves the skull and lower jaw, 1 isolated tooth and a partially preserved postcranial skeleton.
